back: Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Assets turned into cash within a year: inventory, trade receivables, cash.
Debts due within a year: trade payables, overdraft, short-term loans.
Cash → inventory → sales on credit (debtors) → cash.
Cannot pay suppliers, wages or bills; lose credit and sales; may be forced to close.
Idle cash, excess stock (spoilage, storage costs), large debtors (bad debts).
Control stock, collect debts faster, negotiate longer supplier credit, forecast cash, use long-term finance for assets.

front: Transactions that do not change working capital
back: Paying creditors in cash; buying stock on credit; receiving cash from debtors.
The ability to pay short-term debts as they fall due.
